context.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a regional insurer's legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims platform by incrementally migrating claim types to a hybrid cloud architecture. Its core purpose is to maintain continuous claims processing while transitioning workloads to a modern web application.]

## Key Elements
*   [Customers and Brokers]
*   [Claims Adjusters]
*   [Azure Web Application (Container)]
*   [Azure Anti-Corruption Layer / ACL (Container)]
*   [Azure Database with Snapshot State Versioning (Container)]
*   [Azure Observability Container]
*   [On-Premise COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (System of Record)]

## Relationships
*   [Customers and Brokers interact with Azure Web Application via HTTPS/REST for online claim submission]
*   [Claims Adjusters interact with Azure Web Application via HTTPS/REST for claim handling]
*   [Azure Anti-Corruption Layer communicates with On-Premise Mainframe via Secure VPN/ExpressRoute and synchronous REST/MQ APIs]
*   [Azure Web Application authenticates against On-Premise Active Directory via OAuth2/OpenID Connect (SSO)]

## Technology Stack
*   [Azure Cloud (West Europe) with local read-optimized cache for sub-2s UI performance]
*   [Transactional Outbox Pattern for guaranteed at-least-once hybrid message delivery]
*   [JSON Schema / Avro Schema Registry within ACL to prevent mainframe contract violations]
*   [CQRS Pattern to decouple synchronous UI from slow legacy dependencies]
*   [Snapshot State Versioning in Azure database for historical auditability and rollbacks]

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture isolates the rigid, expensive-to-change on-premise mainframe using an Anti-Corruption Layer and asynchronous patterns, protecting system consistency. It accommodates the team's low cloud experience with well-defined C4 boundaries while meeting strict performance, security, and rollback requirements.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a modern, hybrid insurance claims platform that incrementally replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe. It enables online claims submission and adjuster management while maintaining zero data loss and strict legacy interoperability.

## Key Elements
- Customers and Brokers (Users)
- Claims Adjusters (Users)
- Web Application (SPA)
- Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)
- Claim Management Core
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)
- Data Synchronization / ETL Service
- Feature Flag / Routing Service
- Message Broker (Azure Service Bus)
- Cache / Read Model Store
- Observability / Monitoring (Azure Application Insights)
- On-Premise COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (System of Record)
- On-Premise Active Directory

## Relationships
- Customers, Brokers, and Adjusters interact with Web Application via HTTPS/REST (SSO via Active Directory)
- Web Application communicates with Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) via HTTPS/REST
- BFF communicates with Claim Management Core and Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) via HTTPS/REST
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) exchanges data with On-Premise COBOL/DB2 Mainframe via secure mainframe protocols
- Claim Management Core and ACL publish/subscribe events via Azure Service Bus
- Data Synchronization / ETL Service replicates state with On-Premise COBOL/DB2 Mainframe and Cache / Read Model Store

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service: Hosts cloud containers, reducing operational overhead for cloud-inexperienced teams
- Azure Service Bus: Manages asynchronous messaging to isolate hybrid network latency
- Azure Application Insights: Provides centralized observability across cloud and on-premise boundaries
- HTTPS/REST: Standardizes synchronous application and API communication
- Managed Cloud Databases: Provides reliable persistence with automated point-in-time recovery

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe dependencies via an Anti-Corruption Layer and asynchronous messaging, ensuring strict zero-data-loss and one-day rollback constraints. Utilizing managed Azure services minimizes operational complexity for a team with limited cloud experience.

Web Application (SPA).analysis:
## Overview
[Modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurer mainframe claims system by gradually migrating claim types to a cloud platform. The architecture ensures zero claim loss, high performance, and rapid one-day rollbacks.]

## Key Elements
- Customers and Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Web Application (SPA)
- Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)
- On-Premise COBOL/DB2 Mainframe
- On-Premise Active Directory
- Azure Application Insights

## Relationships
- Customers and Brokers -> Web Application (SPA): Interact via HTTPS/REST (SSO via Active Directory)
- Claims Adjusters -> Web Application (SPA): Interact via HTTPS/REST (SSO via Active Directory)
- Web Application (SPA) -> Backend-for-Frontend (BFF): Communicates via HTTPS/REST
- Web Application (SPA) -> On-Premise Active Directory: Authenticates via SSO [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service: Hosts the Web Application (SPA) and BFF due to simplicity for teams with limited cloud experience
- TypeScript & OpenAPI: Generates type-safe API clients to eliminate schema drift between frontend and backend
- Playwright: Executes automated end-to-end smoke tests for rapid claim type rollback verification
- Azure Application Insights: Provides real-time client-side telemetry and performance monitoring

## Rationale
[Optimistic UI updates, strict API contract generation, and feature-flagged routing decouple the modern frontend from slow legacy mainframe responses. This architecture satisfies strict performance, rapid rollback, and security requirements despite the team's limited cloud experience.]

Backend-for-Frontend (BFF).analysis:
## Overview
[System: Insurance Claims Modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe claims system with a modern hybrid cloud architecture.]
[Core Purpose: Orchestrates claim submissions and adjuster workflows while routing data between modern cloud services and the legacy mainframe.]

## Key Elements
- Web Application (SPA)
- Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)
- Claim Management Core
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)
- On-Premise COBOL/DB2 Mainframe
- Azure App Service
- Azure App Configuration
- Azure Application Insights

## Relationships
- Web Application (SPA) -> Backend-for-Frontend (BFF): Communicates via HTTPS/REST
- Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Claim Management Core: Communicates via HTTPS/REST
- Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL): Communicates via HTTPS/REST
- Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Azure App Configuration: Fetches configuration externalization via HTTPS
- Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Azure Application Insights: Exports telemetry and distributed traces via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service: Hosts the BFF as a stateless modular monolith to simplify horizontal scaling for a team with limited cloud experience.
- Azure App Configuration: Externalizes downstream endpoints, timeouts, and feature flags to allow operational adjustments without redeployment.
- Response Caching & Circuit Breakers: Mitigates mainframe latency and prevents cascading failures to meet the sub-2-second performance requirement.
- Correlation IDs & PII Masking Middleware: Ensures distributed tracing across the hybrid boundary while scrubbing sensitive data for security compliance.

## Rationale
[This architecture uses a modular BFF pattern with aggressive caching and circuit breakers to insulate the UI from slow mainframe responses and hybrid network latency.]
[Stateless deployment on Azure App Service and strict API versioning support seamless incremental claim migration and rapid one-day rollback capabilities.]

Claim Management Core.analysis:
## Overview
The Claims Management Core processes modern insurance claims while supporting incremental migration from a 30-year-old mainframe. It ensures high reliability and fast adjuster interfaces in a hybrid cloud environment.

## Key Elements
- Claim Management Core (Azure App Service): Central processing container
- Modular Domain Packages (Auto, Property): Internal bounded contexts
- Outbox Table & Dispatcher: Reliability mechanism for event publishing
- Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous message broker
- ACL Gateway Interface: Boundary mapping to the legacy system
- Cache / Read Model Store: Optimized storage for fast queries

## Relationships
- BFF -> Claim Management Core: Sends HTTPS/REST requests
- Claim Management Core -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes domain events via AMQP
- Claim Management Core -> Cache / Read Model Store: Updates and queries read models via TCP/SQL
- Claim Management Core -> Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL): Translates legacy protocols via secure adapters

## Technology Stack
- Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters): Isolates core business logic from infrastructure
- Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS): Optimizes write consistency and read performance (<2s UI load)
- Mediator Pattern (MediatR): Decouples request handlers within domain modules
- Outbox Pattern & Polly: Ensures zero-data-loss consistency (R-04) and network resilience

## Rationale
This architecture uses proven patterns like CQRS and Hexagonal design to isolate legacy complexity and manage limited cloud experience. It guarantees strict consistency and fast rollbacks without altering the restricted mainframe interfaces.

Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL).analysis:
## Overview
This system modernizes a regional insurer's 30-year-old claims platform by incrementally migrating claim types to Azure while retaining the on-premise mainframe as the system of record. It bridges legacy COBOL/DB2 systems with modern cloud components using an Anti-Corruption Layer to ensure zero data loss, strict security, and high performance.

## Key Elements
- Customers and Brokers (External Users)
- Claims Adjusters (Internal Users)
- On-Premise COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (System of Record)
- On-Premise Active Directory
- Web Application (SPA) (Azure App Service)
- Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) (Azure App Service)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) (Azure App Service)
- Message Broker (Azure Service Bus)
- Cache / Read Model Store (Managed Cloud Database)
- Observability (Azure Application Insights)

## Relationships
- Customers, Brokers, and Adjusters -> Web Application (SPA): Accesses online claim submission and adjuster screens [HTTPS]
- Web Application (SPA) -> Backend-for-Frontend (BFF): Communicates via [HTTPS/REST]
- Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL): Communicates via [HTTPS/REST]
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) -> On-Premise COBOL/DB2 Mainframe: Exchanges data via [Secure Mainframe Protocols]
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) -> Message Broker (Azure Service Bus): Publishes and subscribes events via [Azure Service Bus Protocol]
- Web Application (SPA) -> On-Premise Active Directory: Authenticates via [Single Sign-On / OIDC/OAuth2]

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service: Hosts modern web, BFF, and ACL containers for rapid deployment.
- Azure Service Bus: Provides asynchronous messaging and Outbox pattern support for reliable delivery.
- Managed Cloud Database / Cache: Implements read-through/write-through caching to satisfy sub-2s UI requirements.
- Azure Application Insights: Delivers distributed tracing and metrics instrumentation for hybrid observability.
- Clean Architecture / Ports & Adapters: Organizes ACL internal code to simplify maintenance despite low cloud experience.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe dependencies behind a robust Anti-Corruption Layer while incrementally migrating claim types. It successfully reconciles strict legacy constraints, latency bottlenecks, and zero-data-loss requirements within Azure.

Data Synchronization / ETL Service.analysis:
## Overview
[The Data Synchronization / ETL Service replicates and transforms state between the on-premise mainframe and cloud read models using managed Azure components. It ensures strict consistency and reliable hybrid data pipelines during incremental claim migrations.]

## Key Elements
- Data Synchronization / ETL Service (Azure Compute / ETL)
- On-Premise COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (System of Record)
- Cache / Read Model Store (Managed Cloud Database / Cache)
- Azure Service Bus (Message Broker & DLQ)
- Azure Application Insights (Observability)
- Azure App Configuration (Centralized Configuration Store)

## Relationships
- Data Synchronization / ETL Service -> On-Premise COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (System of Record): Extracts batch data and state via Secure Mainframe Protocols / ETL [ETL / Secure Protocols]
- Data Synchronization / ETL Service -> Cache / Read Model Store: Upserts transformed data and read models via Database Replication [Database Replication]
- Data Synchronization / ETL Service -> Azure Service Bus: Routes failed messages to Dead-Letter Queues (DLQs) using AMQP [AMQP]
- Data Synchronization / ETL Service -> Azure Application Insights: Publishes telemetry, lag metrics, and error rates via HTTPS [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service / Container Instances: Hosts the ETL service with modular adapters, supporting the team's cloud transition.
- Azure Service Bus: Provides resilient message brokering, circuit breakers, and Dead-Letter Queues (DLQs) to handle transient failures within the 23:00–05:00 batch window.
- Azure Application Insights: Delivers real-time observability, SLA tracking, and error logging for pipeline monitoring.
- Azure App Configuration: Stores centralized pipeline parameters, batch sizes, and feature toggles to enable rapid operational adjustments without code deployments.

## Rationale
- The architecture utilizes proven managed cloud tooling and modular adapters to offset the team's limited cloud experience while strictly adhering to the 6-hour batch window constraint.
- Idempotent upserts, automated reconciliation jobs, and bi-directional synchronization triggers guarantee data consistency and support rapid one-day rollbacks for migrated claim types.

Feature Flag / Routing Service.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a Feature Flag and Routing Service that manages incremental claim type migration from a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe to a modern Azure platform. It ensures reliable hybrid routing, rapid rollbacks, and strict consistency without risking data loss.]

## Key Elements
- Feature Flag / Routing Service (Azure App Configuration)
- BFF (Backend-for-Frontend) and Claim Management Core (Azure App Service)
- Routing Client SDK
- Azure Service Bus
- Azure Application Insights

## Relationships
- BFF and Claim Management Core query the Feature Flag / Routing Service using HTTP/REST via the Routing SDK.
- Azure App Configuration publishes cache invalidation events to the BFF via Azure Service Bus.
- BFF and Claim Management Core emit metrics, audit logs, and distributed traces to Azure Application Insights.

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Configuration: Declarative configuration provider for managing routing states with built-in revision history.
- Consistent Hashing: Deterministic algorithm based on claim IDs to guarantee repeatable routing decisions.
- Circuit Breaker Pattern: Implemented in the SDK to enforce fallback-to-safe-default behavior targeting the mainframe during outages.
- Azure Service Bus: Event broker enabling near-instantaneous cache invalidation for emergency rollbacks.
- Azure Application Insights: Observability platform for telemetry, canary evaluation metrics, and distributed tracing.

## Rationale
[Deterministic consistent hashing and explicit overrides ensure compliance with consistency and one-day rollback requirements. Furthermore, using managed cloud configurations and built-in SDK resilience patterns minimizes operational overhead for a team with limited cloud experience.]

## Overview
This system modernizes a regional insurer's 30-year-old claims mainframe by migrating claim types incrementally to an Azure-hosted platform. It ensures reliable hybrid integration while keeping the legacy system as the primary database of record.

## Key Elements
- Customers and Brokers: External users submitting online claims
- Claims Adjusters: Internal users managing claims via the web application
- On-Premise COBOL/DB2 Mainframe: Legacy system of record
- On-Premise Active Directory: Identity provider for Single Sign-On
- Web Application (SPA) & Backend-for-Frontend (BFF): Modern user interface layer
- Claim Management Core: Business logic container for processed claims
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL): Integration bridge translating modern events for the mainframe
- Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous message broker isolating hybrid latency

## Relationships
- Customers/Brokers -> Web Application (SPA): HTTPS / TLS for online claim submission
- Web Application (SPA) -> Backend-for-Frontend (BFF): HTTPS REST / JSON
- Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Claim Management Core: Internal REST / gRPC
- Claim Management Core -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes and subscribes events [AMQP]
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes and subscribes events [AMQP]
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) -> On-Premise COBOL/DB2 Mainframe: Secure Mainframe Protocols

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service: Hosts containerized microservices (BFF, Core, ACL) for rapid deployment
- Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous message broker with outbox pattern and dead-letter queues to guarantee exactly-once processing (R-04)
- Azure Application Insights: Distributed tracing using Correlation IDs across hybrid boundaries
- Azure Active Directory: Single sign-on authentication enforcing enterprise security (R-07)
- Azure Storage: Implements the Valet Key pattern to offload heavy payloads and preserve broker throughput

## Rationale
The hybrid event-driven architecture decouples modern Azure components from legacy mainframe constraints and latency. This ensures safe incremental migration, strict data consistency, and rapid one-day fallback capabilities per claim type.
